name: Uncombable Hair Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of dry, frizzy, and unruly hair that cannot be combed flat
Scanning electron microscopy showing triangular or kidney-shaped hair shafts with longitudinal grooves
Onset of hair abnormalities in infancy or early childhood
No evidence of scalp inflammation or scarring
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of major criteria including characteristic hair shaft abnormalities clinically and confirmed by electron microscopy, with onset in early childhood
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by electron microscopy; genetic testing may identify mutations in PADI3, TGM3, or TCHH genes.

imaging: Scanning electron microscopy revealing characteristic hair shaft abnormalities
other: Clinical examination showing dry, frizzy, uncombable hair
Family history consistent with autosomal inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Beaded hair shaft appearance on microscopy
Twisted hair shafts visible on light microscopy
May be associated with syndromic features
Nodes and fractures along hair shaft
Hair fragility due to physical or chemical trauma
No characteristic triangular hair shaft shape

redFlags: Presence of scalp inflammation or scarring
Rapid hair loss with systemic symptoms
Signs of ectodermal dysplasia or multisystem involvement
references: Rogers M, et al. Uncombable Hair Syndrome: Clinical and Genetic Update. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Patel A, et al. Genetic Basis of Uncombable Hair Syndrome. Clin Genet. 2019.
